title: Janitizer: Rethinking Binary Tools for Practical and Comprehensive Security
problem: Existing binary rewriting techniques for security either lack code coverage or soundness, or incur prohibitive performance overhead. Source-level protections are infeasible when source is unavailable.
motivation: Comprehensive security requires all executable code to be protected; gaps in libraries or third-party code become attack surfaces. Efficient binary-level solutions are essential when source is unavailable.
method: Janitizer combines static analysis with runtime checks to protect compiled binaries. It uses static analysis to examine the code (without running it) and identify where security needs to be added, then places runtime checks (safeguards) at those locations. This hybrid approach provides the performance of static analysis with the correctness of runtime checking. It protects against memory corruption (through memory sanitization) and control flow attacks (through control flow integrity).
key_novelty: Janitizer achieves both comprehensive security and practical performance by combining static analysis with runtime checks in binary rewriting.
contributions: Hybrid static-dynamic mechanism for comprehensive binary security
Sound memory sanitizer with full code coverage
Sound control flow integrity with full code coverage
Performance competitive with low-coverage static techniques while matching dynamic correctness

metrics.other: Comprehensive code coverage with practical performance overhead

limitations: Specific overhead numbers not provided in abstract; evaluation scope not detailed.
primary_theme: Hybrid binary rewriting for sound comprehensive security
